title: Lipase degradation of Dynasan 114 and 116 solid lipid nanoparticles (SLN)--effect of surfactants, storage time and crystallinity.
text_summary: 固体脂质纳米颗粒（SLN）体内药物的释放是通过脂质基质的扩散和降解来实现的。制备了不同结晶度的SLN，研究结晶度对降解速度的影响。生产后，具有较低结晶度基质（Dynasan 114 和 116，NaCh）的 SLN 比较高结晶度颗粒（所有 SLN 均采用 Plx 407）降解得更快，并且在储存期间随着结晶度的增加，降解速度降低。由与非干扰性 Plx 407 稳定的 Dynasan 116 制成的快速结晶颗粒在储存期间显示降解速度没有变化。使用较高结晶脂质与结晶干扰性 NaCh（Dynasan 116，NaCh）结合生产的 SLN 需要“成熟时间”才能达到足够的结晶度。

   Lipase degradation of Dynasan 114 and 116 solid lipid
nanoparticles (SLN)—effect of surfactants, storage time and
                            crystallinity

             Carsten Olbrich, Oliver Kayser, Rainer H. Mu¨ller *

       Department of Pharmaceutics, Biopharmaceutics and Biotechnology, The Free Uni ersity of Berlin, Kelchstrabe 31,
                                          D-12169 Berlin, Germany

                Received 2 January 2001; received in revised form 21 January 2002; accepted 23 January 2002


Abstract

  In vivo drug release from solid lipid nanoparticles (SLN) takes place by diffusion and degradation of the lipid
matrix. SLN with different degree of crystallinity were prepared to study the effect of crystallinity on the degradation
velocity. These SLN were produced by using glycerides with different length of fatty acid chains and known
differences in crystallisation velocity (Dynasan 114 and 116), and using stabilisers interfering differently with the
crystallisation process of the lipid matrix (cholic acid sodium salt (NaCh), Poloxamer 407 (Plx 407)). NaCh disturbs
the crystallisation process, Poloxamer shows little interference. The particles were characterised by photon correlation
spectroscopy (PCS) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), degradation velocity was determined directly after
production and during storage up to 4 weeks under different storage conditions using an especially developed assay
based on the NEFA Test kit. After production, SLN with a lower crystallinity matrix (Dynasan 114 and 116, NaCh)
degraded faster than higher crystalline particles (all SLN with Plx 407), and showed a decrease in degradation velocity
with increasing crystallinity during storage. Fast crystallising particles made from Dynasan 116 stabilised with the
non-interfering Plx 407 showed no change in the degradation velocity during storage. SLN produced with a higher
crystalline lipid in combination with the crystallisation-disturbing NaCh (Dynasan 116, NaCh) required a ‘ripening
time’ to reach sufﬁcient crystallinity. © 2002 Elsevier Science B.V. All rights reserved.


Keywords: SLN; Nanoparticles; Pancreatic lipase; Crystallinity; Dynasan
